newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND SNEAK INTO CHAMPIONS FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND SNEAK INTO CHAMPIONS FINAL.

text.p: New Zealand lost to Pakistan on Wednesday but sneaked into the final of the Singer Champions Trophy cricket tournament after a day of drama and confusion.

New Zealand lost their last league match against Pakistan by four wickets, a result which meant both New Zealand and Sri Lanka finished with three points from four matches. Pakistan topped the table with six points.
Tournament referee Mike Smith, a former England captain, contacted International Cricket Council (ICC) chief executive David Richards to clarify which team should face Pakistan in Friday's final.
They initially agreed run rate should decide it, which would have meant a place in the final for Sri Lanka.
But New Zealand team officials contacted their own board, who, in turn, sought further clarification from the ICC.

Richards then spoke to Ali Bacher, the South African who devised the rule, and they finally decided that New Zealand should go through to the final because they had performed better in the league stages against Sri Lanka. New Zealand beat Sri Lanka once and their other clash ended in a tie.
"The objective is to see which team performed better than the other," Richards said in a press statement.
"Unfortunely, the wording of the rule is ambiguous, as it refers to...the winner of all the preliminary matches played between them...

"That, taken literally, could mean the winner of each and every match...I have spoken to the South African cricket board and they have advised that the wording is the aggregate outcome of all matches played between the two teams."
This meant Wednesday's match had just been a dress-rehearsal for the final.
Pakistan, chasing 193 for victory, achieved the target in 48.3 overs with four wickets in hand.
They got off to a flying start with openers Saeed Anwar and Aamir Sohail hitting a fluent 66 runs in just 63 balls. Anwar scored 54, with six fours and two sixes, and Sohail 25.
Salim Malik (41 off 66 balls) and Moin Khan (37 off 78 balls) saw Pakistan through.

Earlier Waqar Younis had ripped through the tentative New Zealand batting with a haul of six for 44. Spearheading the Pakistan attack in the absence of Wasim Akram, who rested his sore shoulder, he fell just short of his career-best six for 26 achieved against Sri Lanka at Sharjah in 1990.
New Zealand slumped to 60 for six in 12.5 overs but Adam Parore (74) and skipper Lee Germon (53) staged a fine comeback, putting on 115 runs for seventh wicket in 202 balls.
Besides Waqar, who generated a lively pace on a slow wicket, Shahid Nazir had an impressive opening spell, removing openers Bryan Young and Craig Spearman cheaply.
Final league placings (tabulate under played, won, lost, tied, points, net run rate): Pakistan 4 3 1 - 6 -0.20 Sri Lanka 4 1 2 1 3 +0.16
